name: UCW World Championship
epitaph: The Mask beat BG Bomb for it on 5 August 2005 and had it three weeks when the promotion announced an Elimination Chamber to unify it with the Heavyweight Title, then closed its doors instead. He carried the belt to PWE, where Michael Hopkins was introduced as its champion and he introduced himself as the man it had belonged to — an argument about a company nobody in the room had heard of, conducted with a belt that had its holder's name engraved on it.
notes: Sources disagree on who held it after August 2005: The Mask calls it “my World Title” in the same promo that has Hopkins holding it, and PWE's own Underground introduces Hopkins as the UCW World Champion. Both readings are recorded.

name: UCW North American Championship
epitaph: Won by The Mask off Trent Hawk on 15 July 2005 and the only UCW belt that kept being defended after the promotion stopped existing: he retained it against Holden Gilmour on a PWE pay-per-view, then unified it with the IPW Impact Title, and was defending it again against the Prophet when the record ends.

name: UCW Dream Championship
epitaph: Defended in a cage of weapons at Madison Square Garden on 27 November 2005 against three challengers at once and retained by pinfall — the only complete UCW title match anywhere in the surviving record, and it was fought on another promotion's pay-per-view.

name: UCW Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Trent Hawk's, and the belt Ultimate Championship Wrestling was going to put into an Elimination Chamber against its World Title the last time it ran a show. He was still carrying it in August, walking a red carpet into a Foundation of Brutality building where the headmaster took it off him at the door.
notes: The unification match is named only in The Mask's own recollection: “The last time I was in a UCW ring, it was announced that there would be an Elimination Chamber match to unify my World Title, and Trent Hawk's Heavyweight Title.”

name: UCW US Championship
epitaph: The first belt The Mask ever challenged for and the only one he failed to win: Mike Smith beat him for it in the weeks before the North American Title changed hands, and not one other match for it survives anywhere.
notes: The championship is named once, as “US Title match”, inside a run of match lines the same ledger heads with the promotion's own acronym for its other two belts. The full name it was billed under is not recorded; the short form is kept as written.
